title: Transactions and a stable API boundary
summary: Read products through a repository inside a read-only transaction and return a response record.

scenario.briefing: The service injects its repository into a field, returns the JPA entity, and runs no transaction, so lazy fields fail once the entity leaves the session. Move to constructor injection, return a response record, and put the database work in a transaction.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: The repository interface is already declared at the bottom of the file.
Declare the repository as a private final field and assign it in the constructor.
Annotate the read method with @Transactional(readOnly = true).
Build a ProductResponse from the entity id, name, and stock instead of returning the entity.

misconceptions.description: Holding a database transaction during a remote call.
misconceptions.feedback: The transaction keeps a connection checked out. Call remote services before or after the transactional method.
Constructor injection makes the dependency final and visible in the constructor signature.

misconceptions.description: Returning the entity from the service.
misconceptions.feedback: The entity is tied to the table. Map it to a response record at the API boundary.

sections.title: Entities belong to the data layer
sections.body: An @Entity class maps to a table. Its fields follow the schema, and lazy relationships may load only while a session is open. Returning it from a service couples the API to the table and can serialize fields that clients should never see. Map it to a response record at the boundary.

sections.title: Repositories remove boilerplate
sections.body: A repository interface that extends JpaRepository<Product, Long> gets CRUD operations and derived queries such as findByStockGreaterThan without an implementation class. Spring creates the proxy at startup.

sections.title: Transactions define the unit of work
sections.body: Spring wraps a method annotated with @Transactional in a transaction. readOnly = true lets the provider skip dirty checking for reads. The transaction belongs to the service method that owns the database work, not to a controller that also calls remote services.

sections.title: Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit
sections.body: A final field assigned in the constructor cannot be replaced after construction and is checked by the compiler. Field injection hides the dependency and makes the class harder to build in a test.

vocabulary.definition: A class whose fields map to columns of a database table.
An interface that gives the service CRUD and query methods for an entity.
A unit of work that commits together or rolls back together.
A small immutable type that defines what the API returns.
Supplying dependencies through a constructor so they can be final.

steps.title: Close the data boundary
steps.prompt: Edit ProductService.java. Use constructor injection, keep the entity and repository mapped, mark reads transactional, and return a ProductResponse instead of the entity. Run the checks when done.

tests.description: The service receives its repository through the constructor.
The entity is mapped and exposed through a Spring Data repository.
Reads run inside a read-only transaction.
The public method returns a response record, not the entity.
includes: record ProductResponse(long id, String name, int stock)

steps.title: Review the transaction boundary
steps.prompt: Review the controller and select every real problem.

artifact.title: ProductController.java
artifact.caption: The controller injects by field, returns the entity, and keeps a database transaction open during a remote pricing call.

findings.label: The endpoint returns the JPA entity as the response body.
The controller uses field injection for ProductService.
The transaction stays open while the remote pricing call runs.
Marking the method read-only would make the remote call safe inside the transaction.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the entity boundary, injection, and transaction scope are fixed.
The code only needs formatting changes.
Ship it; the remote call inside a transaction is acceptable.

steps.explanation: Returning the entity couples the API to the table and can serialize lazy fields. Field injection hides the dependency, and @Transactional holds a database connection while an external HTTP call runs. Return a response record, inject through the constructor, and move the remote call outside the transaction.
